title_en: Opinion of the Supreme People's Court on Strengthening the Work of Presidents and Division Chiefs of People's Courts at All Levels in Handling Cases (For Trial Implementation)
keywords_en: Handling of cases by presidents and division chiefs of people's courts at all levels
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Opinion on Strengthening the Work of Court Presidents and Division Heads in Handling Cases at People's Courts at All Levels (Trial Implementation)

Fa Fa [2017] No. 10

In order to fully implement the judicial accountability system, optimize the allocation of trial resources, and give full play to the exemplary, leading, and guiding role of court presidents and division heads at people's courts at all levels in trial work, in accordance with the Notice of the Central Political and Legal Affairs Commission on Strictly Implementing the Selection Standards and Procedures for Judges and Prosecutors, the Several Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Improving the Judicial Accountability System of People's Courts, and other relevant provisions, and in light of the actual trial work, the following opinions are put forward regarding strengthening the work of court presidents and division heads in handling cases:

1. After being appointed as judges within the quota system, court presidents and division heads at people's courts at all levels shall handle cases, including hearing cases alone, participating in a collegial panel as the judge in charge of the case, participating in a collegial panel as the presiding judge or as a member of the collegial panel. It is prohibited to not handle cases, delegate case handling, or handle cases in name only after entering the quota. Handling cases by means such as listening to reports, reviewing documents in writing, or approving cases shall not be used as a substitute for actual case handling.

2. Court presidents and division heads at people's courts at all levels shall handle cases based on the trial work they oversee, taking into account their professional backgrounds and personal expertise, and shall focus on hearing major, difficult, complex, and new-type cases, as well as cases that have general guiding significance in the application of law.

3. Court presidents and division heads at people's courts at all levels shall, as the judge in charge of the case, handle a certain number of cases. Matters such as presiding over or participating in professional judge meetings and the adjudication committee, coordinating and supervising major sensitive cases, receiving visitors, and directing enforcement shall be included in the workload and incorporated into performance assessment, but shall not be used to offset the number of cases handled.

4. The annual number of cases handled by division heads at grassroots and intermediate people's courts shall reach 50% to 70% of the average number of cases handled by judges in their respective divisions.

The annual number of cases handled by the president of a grassroots people's court shall reach 5% to 10% of the average number of cases handled by judges in that court, and that for other court leaders within the quota shall reach 30% to 40% of the average number of cases handled by judges in that court.

The annual number of cases handled by the president of an intermediate people's court shall reach 5% of the average number of cases handled by judges in that court, and that for other court leaders within the quota shall reach 20% to 30% of the average number of cases handled by judges in that court.

Grassroots and intermediate people's courts may, based on the situation of case filings and closures in their respective courts and in light of the need to complete trial work tasks, appropriately increase the number of cases independently handled or participated in by court presidents and division heads in their courts above the minimum standards set forth in this Opinion.

The minimum standards for the number of cases handled by court presidents and division heads at high people's courts and the Supreme People's Court shall be separately stipulated by the high people's courts and the Supreme People's Court.

People's courts at all levels shall comprehensively consider factors such as the court level, leadership positions, areas of responsibility, the workload of trial management and supervision affairs and administrative affairs undertaken, comprehensively apply methods such as case weight coefficients to calculate the average number of cases handled, reasonably determine the annual requirements for the number of cases independently handled or participated in by court presidents and division heads, and make this information public in the office and case handling system. The minimum standards for the number of cases handled shall be adjusted in a timely manner based on changes in trial work tasks, the number of judges in the quota, and the allocation of auxiliary personnel.

5. People's courts at all levels shall establish a working mechanism to ensure that court presidents and division heads handle cases. For grassroots people's courts that have implemented trial team reform, division heads and deputy division heads shall be directly incorporated into trial teams to assume the trial and supervision responsibilities for relevant cases; they shall explore the incorporation of court presidents, vice presidents, and other court leaders within the quota into corresponding trial teams to hear cases.

People's courts at all levels shall, based on actual circumstances, equip court presidents and division heads with necessary judge assistants and clerks, so that court presidents and division heads can concentrate on core trial tasks such as holding court sessions, evaluating cases, and drafting judgments.

People's courts at all levels shall strictly implement the Provisions on Protecting Judicial Personnel in Lawfully Performing Their Statutory Duties and the measures for its implementation, actively seek support from local Party committees and governments, further streamline meetings and documents, compress management processes, and ensure that court presidents and division heads have more time and energy to devote to case handling work.

6. The assignment of cases to court presidents and division heads shall primarily be through designated assignment. People's courts at all levels shall improve the mechanism for screening and diverting cases at the case filing stage, and promote the priority assignment of major, difficult, complex, new-type cases, and cases with general significance in the application of law to court presidents and division heads for trial. For particularly major, difficult, and complex cases, a collegial panel may be formed in accordance with the law by the court president, vice presidents, and members of the adjudication committee to hear the case.

7. When court presidents and division heads at people's courts at all levels handle cases, they shall play an exemplary, leading, and guiding role. Court presidents and division heads are encouraged to hold demonstration trials and to increase the live broadcast of trials for cases handled by court presidents and division heads. When handling cases, court presidents and division heads shall also pay attention to summarizing trial work experience, unifying the standards for adjudication, and standardizing and guiding trial work.

8. The completion of case handling tasks by court presidents and division heads at people's courts at all levels shall be subject to public supervision. The trial management department of each high people's court shall be responsible for the annual calculation and verification of the number of cases handled by court presidents and division heads in the courts within its jurisdiction, and shall report monthly on the completion of case handling tasks by the court presidents, vice presidents, full-time members of the adjudication committee, and other court leaders within the quota in the courts within its jurisdiction, including the number of cases handled, the type of cases, the trial procedures, the method of participation, the number of court sessions held, and the trial quality. The trial management department of each court shall be responsible for the calculation and verification of the number of cases handled by division heads and deputy division heads in its own court and for regular reporting.

Higher-level people's courts shall regularly supervise the case handling situation of court presidents and division heads in lower-level people's courts, issue notices for those who fail to meet the standards, and once problems such as delegated case handling or nominal case handling are discovered, they shall be seriously investigated and held accountable.

9. The performance of court presidents and division heads at people's courts at all levels in handling cases shall be included in the scope of evaluation and supervision of their work. If the annual case handling performance of a court president or division head fails to meet the assessment standards, they shall withdraw from the judge quota. If a court president or division head needs to reduce their annual case handling tasks due to undertaking important special work, coordinating and supervising major sensitive cases, or other reasons, they shall report to the next higher-level people's court for approval and record.

10. For the purposes of this Opinion, "court presidents and division heads" include, unless otherwise specifically stated, court presidents, vice presidents, full-time members of the adjudication committee, other court leaders within the quota, division heads, deputy division heads, and other heads of trial (enforcement) business departments who have a trial title and have entered the judge quota.

11. This Opinion shall be interpreted by the Supreme People's Court.

12. This Opinion shall be implemented on a trial basis from May 1, 2017. Any normative documents previously issued by the Supreme People's Court that are inconsistent with this Opinion shall no longer apply.

April 10, 2017
